newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand firmed to its strongest level in a month on Thursday, helped by dollar selling by offshore players who were upbeat about Wednesday's budget presentation, local traders said.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was quoted at 4.3940/3970 against the dollar compared with 4.4170/4200 overnight.
Dealers said the rand drew its initial impetus from New York-based selling overnight as well as early morning selling out of the East and Europe.
That helped the currency to a day's strongest level of 4.39 bid by 0635 GMT.
But importers, keen to cover at a rand/dollar rate last seen on February 13, came in at the 4.39 level to buy dollars and took the rand up to its weakest level on the day of 4.4045 bid.
"We saw a fair bit of demand below 4.40 from local importers and then we saw more dollars coming in from offshore," a trader said.

Dealers said sentiment on the market continued to be buoyed by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget announcement, pointing specifically to his announcement on the further relaxation of exchange controls.

They said the rand looked set to target the 4.38 level on Friday, although some traders felt the Reserve Bank was likely to use any further strengthening as an opportunity to buy dollars in an effort to reverse the oversold position on its forward book.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals has said he expects the oversold position on its forward book, which stood at around $20 billion last month, to decrease sharply this year.
Dealers said that if the rand managed to break below the 4.38 level, technical factors indicated it could strengthen to the 4.33 level, with 4.30 a possible target thereafter.
Against the crosses, the rand was little changed against sterling at 7.0239/0331 and at 0.3863/3867 marks.
The bond market's performance was less exuberant as some players expressed concern about whether government would be able to achieve its sharp reduction in spending.
Manuel said on Monday expenditure in 1997/98 was budgeted at 189.75 billion rand -- a mere 6.1 percent increase on last year's figure.

Traders also expressed concern about weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market where the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury moved above the 6.90 percent level following a strong set of U.S. economic indicators.
The key R150 was last pegged at a 14.66 percent yield from 14.74 percent on Wednesday after trading in a 14.59 to 14.68 percent range on the day.
Dealers said that as the budget had now been largely priced into the market, attention was likely to shift to continuing pressures on the money market.

"We have come down a long way and could move back up to the 15.00 to 15.25 percent level," a trader said, although another trader said demand was expected to surface if the R150 moved above 15 percent.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage higher at 11.223 billion rand on Wednesday from 11.147 billion rand on Tuesday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners were net buyers of 554.24 billion rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 525.13 million rand's on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at a hefty 16.25 billion rand from 6.4 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
